name: Chornohora Ridge
description: Ukraine's highest mountain ridge, from Zaroslyak over Hoverla to Pip Ivan. Distances are approximate.

zaroslyak.name: Zaroslyak
zaroslyak.text: The trail starts at the old base in the spruce forest.

hoverla.name: Hoverla
hoverla.text: 2061 m, the highest point of Ukraine.

breskul.name: Breskul
breskul.text: The ridge opens up in front of you.

pozhyzhevska.name: Pozhyzhevska
pozhyzhevska.text: Meadows on both sides, wind in your face.

nesamovyte.name: Lake Nesamovyte
nesamovyte.text: Legend says a stone thrown into this lake brings a storm. Better not.

pip-ivan.name: Pip Ivan
pip-ivan.text: The White Elephant observatory stands on the summit. You walked the whole ridge!

story.treeline: The spruces thin out. Above you there is only grass and sky.
story.ridge-wind: Up here the wind never stops. You zip up your jacket and walk on.
story.white-elephant: Far ahead, a grey building shows on the summit: the old observatory.

facts.six-2000: Chornohora holds six of Ukraine's peaks above 2000 m: Hoverla, Brebeneskul, Pip Ivan, Petros, Hutyn Tomnatyk and Rebra.
facts.prut: The Prut, one of the big rivers of Ukraine and Moldova, starts as a stream on the slopes of Hoverla.
facts.border-posts: Between the world wars this ridge was the border between Poland and Czechoslovakia. The numbered stone posts still stand along the path.
facts.polonyna: A polonyna is a high mountain meadow. Every summer Hutsul shepherds drove flocks up here and lived in wooden huts until autumn.
facts.reserve: Much of Chornohora is protected by the Carpathian Biosphere Reserve and the Carpathian National Nature Park.
facts.cirques: Lakes Nesamovyte and Brebeneskul lie in cirques: bowls carved by glaciers that covered these mountains in the last ice age.
facts.observatory: The observatory on Pip Ivan was built by Poland in 1936–1938 for astronomy and weather studies. Locals nicknamed it the White Elephant.

quiet-stones.name: No Panic
quiet-stones.description: Reach Lake Nesamovyte without throwing a single stone.
